title: Official talk
job: Announcements, offices and counters: the formal register you hear
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: THE -(seu)pnida LEVEL IS DEFERENTIAL, NOT MERELY POLITE. It is what a clerk says to you and what you say in a formal setting. Moving it into a chat with a friend is as wrong as putting -yo into a station announcement.

FOUR ENDINGS, ONE LEVEL: -(seu)pnida states, -(seu)pnikka asks, -(eu)sipsio orders and -(eu)psida proposes. Every -yo sentence you already own has a twin up here, and the level is chosen for the room, not for the sentence.

-(eu)psida IS DOWNWARD OR AMONG EQUALS, never to an elder, a customer or a superior. English let us reads as neutral and this does not: upward, the proposal stays L2-M6's -(eu)llaeyo with the honorific.

THE STEM DECIDES THE SHAPE. A vowel stem takes -mnida (hamnida, gamnida) and a consonant stem takes -seumnida (isseumnida, eopseumnida). The n is written because it is what you hear: hap-nida is said hamnida.

L3-M8's HONORIFIC SITS UNDERNEATH THE LEVEL. -si- goes on first and the level goes on after it, which gives -(eu)sipnida on paper and -(eu)simnida as it is said: sajangnim-kkeseo osimnida. This course writes the second, as it writes hamnida. The honorific system is reused whole and not extended here.

ENGLISH HAS NO SPEECH LEVEL, so a learner who is spoken to in -mnida answers in -mnida. Do not. Understand the announcement and answer at your own level, which is -yo, and the exchange is correct on both sides.

THE FOUR FROZEN PHRASES STAY FROZEN. gamsahamnida, mannaseo bangapseumnida, joesonghamnida and jal meogeosseumnida were learnt whole; nothing here rebuilds them, and none of the new forms points back at them.
THE -a/eo juda AUXILIARY STAYS JOINED, as it is on L2-M1's and L2-M7's rows. So the formal request is gidaryeojusipsio in one piece, never gidaryeo jusipsio.

words.note: The formal command: L2-M8's gidaryeoyo, the joined -a/eo juda auxiliary, the honorific -si-, then -psio. The -yo twin you already own is gidaryeojuseyo.

sentences.trap: You hear this constantly and almost never say it. -(eu)sipsio is issued from behind a counter; the customer's version stays gidaryeojuseyo.
sentences.sound: JAM-si-man GI-da-ryeo-ju-SIP-si-o. The last four syllables run flat and fast.

variations.changed: your own level, which is what you would say back
a place instead of a length of time

mistake.why: This course writes the -a/eo juda auxiliary joined to the verb, exactly as it did at L2-M1 and L2-M7. Splitting it here would make one word into two.

sentences.usage: Heard at a bank counter, a ticket window and on the phone.
sentences.mnemonic: -sipsio comes from the other side of the glass.

words.note: The desk where a form or an application is handed in. Said jeop-su, with the p held.
The window itself. -imnida is the formal copula, the twin of L1-M5's -ieyo, and it attaches to the noun the same way.

sentences.trap: -imnida is not a stronger -ieyo. It is a different level, so it belongs on the sign and in the announcement, not in the answer you give the person beside you.

variations.changed: which counter it is
a verb instead of the copula

mistake.why: Correct Korean at the wrong level. On a notice or from staff on duty the copula is -imnida; -yeyo would read as a colleague mentioning it in passing.

sentences.usage: A sign above a window, or a guard pointing.

words.note: One syllable, aspirated: a puff of air on the p.
L1-M3's isseoyo at the formal level. A consonant stem takes -seumnida, and the written p of -seup is said as m before the n.

sentences.trap: Do not hunt for a formal word meaning to be. It is the same verb; only the ending has moved up a level.
sentences.sound: PYO-neun YEO-gi-e I-sseum-ni-da. The middle of isseumnida is a held ss.

variations.changed: the level you would answer at
a different subject

mistake.why: -(seu)pnikka is the question ending. Used to state something it turns the notice into a question nobody asked.

sentences.usage: A clerk answering where something is kept.

sentences.cue: There are no tickets at the moment.

words.note: L1-M3's eopseoyo at the formal level. Korean has a whole verb for not existing, so the negative particle an never appears with it.

sentences.trap: an isseumnida is not the negative. eopda is its own verb, and putting an in front of the positive one is the commonest way to say this wrongly.

variations.cue: There are no tickets at the moment.
variations.changed: the level, as a colleague would say it
today rather than right now

mistake.why: Korean does not negate isseumnida; it swaps the verb for eopseumnida. The same rule you learnt at L1-M3 survives the change of level.

sentences.usage: The sentence that closes a ticket window.
sentences.mnemonic: No an — a different verb entirely.

sentences.cue: There will be an announcement shortly.

words.note: The bare noun inside L2-M7's jamsiman. Without -man it is simply a short while, and it takes L4-M6's hu-e to make shortly.
The word on every information desk. annae bangsong is the public announcement itself.
Anything sent out over a speaker: the platform, the shop, the radio.

sentences.trap: A Korean announcement states a fact in the present or plain future, not with a promise ending. isseumnida already carries there will be.

variations.changed: what happens after the moment
your own report of it, at your own level

mistake.why: -man means only and belongs with a request to wait. In front of hu-e the noun stands bare: jamsi hu-e.

sentences.usage: Heard on a platform or in a department store.
sentences.mnemonic: jamsi is the moment, jamsiman asks for it.

words.note: Used only in announcements and notices; the person in front of you is a saram or a sonnim, never a seunggaek.
The honorific plural you address a crowd with. It opens the announcement and is followed by a comma and the formal level.
A noun that takes hada to become a verb. L4-M9 borrows it for journeys and adds nothing to it.

sentences.trap: yeoreobun is not the plural of you. It is a way of addressing a room, so it never turns up in a two-person conversation.

variations.cue: Passengers, the train is departing now.
variations.changed: now, said as the doors close
your own report afterwards, at your own level

mistake.why: yeoreobun opens a formal address, so the sentence has to finish at that level. -yo after it sounds like a friend shouting across the platform.

sentences.cue: The train arrives at ten o'clock.

words.note: The partner of chulbal, and built the same way with hada. The k meeting h is said as one aspirated sound.

sentences.trap: The clock inside an announcement is still L2-M6's: native numbers for the hour, si for the hour, bun for the minute. Nothing about the level changes the counting.

variations.changed: past, and at your own level
a different hour

mistake.why: The question ending on a timetable. -(seu)pnikka asks; a board and a loudspeaker state, so they end in -(seu)pnida.

words.note: Two layers in order: L3-M8's honorific -si- first, then the formal level. The -yo twin you already own is oseyo.

sentences.trap: The honorific and the level are separate decisions. -si- honours the person in the sentence; -mnida honours the room, and a sentence can carry one without the other.

variations.changed: the other verb of the pair
a different person being honoured

mistake.why: -kkeseo has already marked the subject as honoured, so dropping -si- from the verb contradicts the particle in the same sentence.

sentences.usage: An assistant telling a waiting visitor.

sentences.cue: I will handle the registration. Do you have ID?

words.note: hada at the formal level. A vowel stem takes -mnida, and the question is the same word with -nikka: hamnikka.
The question twin of isseumnida. Korean changes the ending rather than the word order, so nothing moves to the front.

sentences.trap: You are asked this at the level, and you answer at yours: ne, isseoyo. Matching the clerk's -mnida is the mistake this module exists to stop.

variations.changed: the object particle rather than the topic
the question on its own, as it is usually heard

mistake.why: Perfectly polite, and wrong for the desk. On duty, behind a counter, staff use the formal level; -yo here reads as somebody helping out informally.

sentences.usage: A counter clerk opening a transaction.

words.note: -(eu)psida proposes, but only downward or among equals. Said to a customer or an elder it is rude, and the upward version is L2-M6's -(eu)llaeyo with -si-.

sentences.trap: English let us is neutral and this is not. A teacher may say it to a class; a student may not say it back.

variations.changed: without the address to the room
a different proposal

mistake.why: Proposing upward with -(eu)psida. To a superior the invitation goes through -(eu)sillaeyo, and the formal ending here makes the presumption worse, not better.

sentences.usage: A chair opening a meeting, or a teacher starting a lesson.

comprehensionPool.cue: There will be an announcement shortly.
The train arrives at ten o'clock.
The tickets are at the reception counter.
There are no tickets at the moment.
